claims.text: The target material is an equimolar (MoWVNbTa)S2 high-entropy transition-metal dichalcogenide.
The five dithiocarbamate precursors form a molecular-scale homogeneous mixture of Mo, W, V, Nb, and Ta.
Thermolysis at 500 °C for 1 hour under argon will form a nanostructured high-entropy 2D metal disulfide powder.
SPS at 1000 °C for 15 minutes under 30 MPa will densify the sulfide while retaining its high-entropy configuration.
A thermolysis window of 450–500 °C ensures complete ligand decomposition while avoiding oxide formation and incomplete decomposition.
Sintering at 1000 °C produces full densification without phase separation or excessive grain growth.
The processed material will have a dual-phase microstructure combining a B2-ordered solid-solution matrix with a retained 2H-layered structure.
Atomic-size mismatch among Mo, W, V, Nb, and Ta causes severe lattice distortion within the 2H-MoS2 lattice.
Nb solute stabilizes or enhances a B2-ordered matrix in the target sulfide.
The molecular-precursor route prevents elemental segregation and promotes a single-phase high-entropy solid solution.
Severe lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion will increase the hardness and yield strength of the target material.
Nb and the 2H structure promote a protective Nb2O5/Ta2O5 scale during high-temperature exposure.
A dense, defect-rich microstructure limits aqueous-corrosion pathways.
The processed (MoWVNbTa)S2 material will exceed 450 HV in Vickers hardness.
SPS will give the target material a density approaching its theoretical maximum.
The target material will have a lower aqueous corrosion-current density than a standard FeCoCrNi HEA.
The target material will retain a stable oxide scale after exposure to air at 800 °C.
An unreinforced FeCoCrNi matrix has a microhardness of approximately 268 HV, while a 30 wt.% WC-reinforced composite reaches approximately 459 HV, a 71.2% increase.
Processing significantly above 1000 °C may transform the 2H phase or relax lattice distortion, whereas processing below 450 °C leaves incompletely decomposed precursors.

contradictions.description: The initial state says the precursors are dissolved in an organic solvent, but the intervention describes the thermolysis as solventless without specifying solvent removal.

The hypothesis proposes a dual-phase B2/2H microstructure, while the mechanism and falsification rule require a single-phase solid solution or phase-pure product. It is therefore unclear whether observation of both proposed phases would confirm or falsify the hypothesis.

The same matrix is described both as a B2-ordered structure and as a 2H-layered MoS2 lattice. These are distinct crystal-structure descriptions, and their proposed coexistence or spatial partitioning is not defined.
